presentation_rule: Forecast, then Key Assumptions of at most 150 words, then downloads. Supporting research belongs in downloads. Presentation changes do not refresh model dates or estimates.

1723.caption: ¥ billion, except EPS and margins · G = company guidance; E = JII estimate
1723.forecast_notes: FY3/27 is company guidance. FY3/28 sales and OP match the company’s medium-term targets; its net income and EPS are JII calculations. FY3/29–30 are JII estimates.
bullets: Sales: ¥51.5bn in FY3/27, then ¥52bn, ¥54.5bn and ¥57bn. FY3/28 uses the company’s medium-term sales target; subsequent growth is JII’s assumption.

Margins: 24.27%, 25.00%, 24.80% and 24.60%. FY3/28 OP matches the company’s ¥13bn target. Later margins are JII estimates; the model assumes easing without separately quantifying its underlying cost or pricing changes.

EPS: net income remains 69.6% of OP, using the FY3/27 guidance ratio. Weighted shares stay at 63.741m, so future buybacks do not contribute to EPS growth. Delivery, pricing or costs differing from these sales and margin assumptions would change the forecast.

1969.caption: JII base-case estimates in every year · ¥ billion, except EPS and margins
1969.forecast_notes: E = JII estimate. FY3/27 combines actual H1 and estimated H2. Recurring EPS excludes identified security gains and impairment; it differs from reported or company-guided EPS. Cash/debt are year-end balances. Forecast cash flows start from September actual balances; full-year cash-flow totals include disclosed H1.
bullets: Delivery: FY3/27 uses available backlog and incoming orders with the prior H2 financial recognition rate of 35.79%. Later real throughput grows 4% annually; price/mix adds 2%. These are financial proxies, not physical capacity disclosures.

Costs: direct unit costs rise 2%; pay rises 5% with staffing up 2%. Other overhead has 3% inflation and 2% scope growth. Historical H2 expense seasonality is retained. These budgets determine margins; no margin path is imposed.
EPS: prospective tax is 32.29%, with separate minority claims and no unexecuted buybacks. The tax treatment of identified exceptional items remains a material sensitivity.

Funding: seasonal working capital, tax/bonus payments and dividend timing require ¥13.80bn of new FY3/27 borrowing in the base. This funding is uncommitted; slower collections or less financing would change the outcome.
1969.update_note: We will update this model after the announcement to reflect the new results.

1980.caption: JII base-case estimates in every year · ¥ billion, except EPS and margins
1980.forecast_notes: E = JII estimate. FY3/27 OP of ¥48.10bn compares with company guidance of ¥42.00bn. Recurring EPS excludes identified exceptional gains and differs from reported or company-guided EPS.
bullets: Profit retention: the base carries forward the full observed improvement in like-for-like half-year cash gross margin, consistent with improved bidding and execution. This is the most important judgment: retaining half would reduce FY3/30 EPS from ¥319 to about ¥297.
Delivery: staffing grows 5.03% annually, anchored to the latest full-year group headcount increase; productivity adds 1% from FY3/28. These are JII capacity proxies, not disclosed physical output.
Pricing and costs: new bids and nonlabor inputs rise 4% annually; pay rises 5%, informed by the disclosed three-year base-pay increase. Existing bids retain their original prices.
Margins and EPS: overhead grows faster than sales, easing OP margin from 17.5% to 17.0%. The model uses a 31.01% normalized tax rate, separate minority claims and no unexecuted buybacks.

5842.caption: JII conditional base-case estimates · ¥ billion, except EPS · December year ends
5842.forecast_notes: E = JII estimate; FY12/26 earnings combine actual nine months and estimated Q4. Fee-only EPS excludes carry and investment returns; total EPS includes them conditionally. Investment cash use covers Q4 only in FY12/26, then full years. Cash/debt are year-end balances; the separate tax-reserve row deducts the modeled deferred-tax reserve.
bullets: Fees: a 2% management-fee proxy follows the latest quarter’s implied rate. Existing fee exposure declines as funds harvest; fixed cash costs rise 7.12% annually, reducing fee earnings before new fundraising.

Successor fund: the base assumes an unannounced ¥250bn fund closes in 2029 and earns half-year fees. Without it, FY12/29 fee-only EPS is about ¥18.53 instead of ¥63.37. This is the key conditional assumption.
Carry: additional realizations of ¥1bn in Q4, then ¥4bn/¥6bn/¥7bn, draw on the ¥23.2bn unrealized pool. Investment marks are flat; neither carry timing nor returns are recurring fee income.

Funding: annual net investment cash use is ¥6.5bn before successor-fund calls. The base needs ¥0.36bn of uncommitted borrowing in 2029. Cash after the deferred-tax reserve is negative; displayed cash is not distributable surplus.
5842.update_note: We will update this model after the announcement to reflect the new results.

6184.caption: JII base-case estimates · ¥ billion, except EPS and margins
6184.forecast_notes: E = JII estimate; FY1/27 combines actual H1 and estimated H2. Basic EPS retains known H1 exceptional items; none recur in future estimates. ¹ Cash flows cover full fiscal years. Operating FCF deducts cash capex and long-term prepaid investment.
bullets: Growth: seven business lines are forecast separately. FY1/28–30 care revenue growth slows from 30% to 20%, municipal services from 23% to 18%, funerals from 16% to 12%, and graves from 9% to 7%. H1 referrals, sales and municipal partnerships anchor these JII estimates.

Margins: advertising follows noninsurance sales; wages rise 3%, with hiring responding to the care/municipal mix. Other costs rise by 2% inflation plus 60% of incremental activity growth. Costs grow more slowly than revenue, lifting margins.
Investment: annual cash capex rises from ¥0.60bn to ¥0.75bn; software spending feeds depreciation rather than becoming a free earnings benefit.
EPS: future tax is 31.5% before nondeductible goodwill. Separate minority claims and 41.195m basic shares are retained; no new acquisition or buyback is assumed.

6617.caption: JII base-case estimates · ¥ billion, except EPS and margins
6617.forecast_notes: E = JII estimate; FY3/27 combines actual H1 and estimated H2. Recurring EPS excludes identified one-offs. ¹ Cash flows cover full fiscal years; operating FCF deducts cash capex and excludes property proceeds. Estimates retain an after-rent basis; the future lease-accounting effect is unquantified.
bullets: Deliveries: Power orders and real-workload capacity grow 4.5% annually after FY3/27. Backlog conversion is constrained by engineering, testing and acceptance. Metering order growth slows to 3%/2%/1% as the replacement cycle matures; these are JII financial proxies.

Margins: Power/Metering new-order prices rise 2%/1.5%, versus 1.5% input inflation. Old contracts keep vintage prices. Fixed costs rise about 3%; corporate spending and depreciation increase. Slower metering growth and these costs weigh on later OP.
Investment and cash: capex is ¥6.5bn/¥7.5bn/¥7.0bn/¥6.5bn. The estimated ¥8.188bn remaining property receipt in FY3/28 is outside operating FCF; final consideration is undisclosed.
EPS: tax is 31.5%; weighted shares fall from 15.583m to 15.400m, then stay flat. No additional buyback is assumed.

9037.caption: JII base-case estimates · ¥ billion, except EPS and margins · Pre-adoption lease basis
9037.forecast_notes: E = JII estimate; FY3/27 earnings and cash flows combine disclosed H1 and modeled H2. Recurring EPS excludes identified settlement and acquisition-advisory costs. FCF deducts cash capex and finance-lease principal, before dividends, acquisitions and bank repayments. Cash is year-end cash equivalents; longer deposits are separate, not proven restricted. Future lease-standard effects remain unquantified.
bullets: Revenue: existing center/trucking activity is flat. Center wins add 4.5% of prior-year sales against 1% churn; center/trucking prices rise 2%/2.2%. These consolidated financial proxies do not isolate Gunma’s additional consolidation contribution.

Costs: wages rise 3.5%, other variable inputs 1.5%; center/truck productivity improves 1.4%/1.7%. The identified ¥263m acquisition fee is removed once from recurring earnings and the cost anchor. Ordinary depreciation and acquisition goodwill have separate schedules.

Investment: dated construction-payment estimates leave ¥9.63bn of named-project cash after September. Actual payment progress is undisclosed; full building costs still enter depreciation when commissioned. Maintenance and discretionary spending remain separate.

EPS and funding: tax is 33.5%, with separate minority claims and no future buybacks. September cash equivalents are ¥23.62bn; bank repayments are ¥3.5bn annually. Operating rents remain expensed; these are economic forecasts before the new lease standard.

9211.caption: JII conditional base-case estimates · ¥ billion, except EPS and margins
9211.forecast_notes: E = JII estimate; FY12/26 combines actual nine months and estimated Q4. Recurring EPS excludes identified valuation income and impairment, retains other unclassified actual items, and precedes unquantified minority-buyout accretion. No future unclassified operating gain is assumed. Seller payments cover Q4 only in FY12/26, then full years; cash/debt are year-end balances.
bullets: Growth: Q4 activity rises 2.5% from the Q3 financial base, then 6% annually; price/mix adds 1.5% annually. Existing consolidated businesses are retained, with no new M&A.

Costs: variable inputs rise 2.5% and fixed cash costs 5.5%; 60% of the cost pool responds to activity. No future unclassified operating gain is repeated. The separate tax treatment of valuation income and impairment materially affects starting EPS.

Seller obligations: the ¥4.79bn aggregate liability is an imperfect cash-payment proxy. The ¥750m fixed AI ONE price is separately funded as assumed unpaid. Actual settlement status, terms and earnings ownership remain uncertain.

Funding and EPS: the base assumes borrowing can return to the observed ¥12.32bn ceiling; this is uncommitted. Tighter capacity causes dilution. Minority-buyout accretion is excluded until earnings ownership is evidenced, and appears only as a conditional sensitivity.
9211.update_note: We will update this model after the announcement to reflect the new results.
